top_five.text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak has expanded to 7,200 confirmed cases and 3,475 deaths, with ongoing violence in eastern conflict zones severely impeding containment efforts.
Successive major floods in Pakistan have uprooted 40 million people from their communities and caused approximately 7,000 deaths, escalating a protracted humanitarian displacement crisis.
Severe flooding across Nepal has left over 1,385 people confirmed dead and 5,130 missing while destroying critical hydropower infrastructure, prompting emergency electricity exports from India.
A renewed Houthi offensive along Yemen's Red Sea coast has displaced over 82,000 people in a single month, as independent reports document 576 civilian casualties from recent US airstrikes.
Israeli airstrikes in Gaza killed six UN agency staff at a shelter for displaced families and injured at least 21 Palestinians, further disrupting essential aid delivery and civil services.

Middle East.headline: Report Details 500+ Yemeni Civilian Casualties From 2023-25 US Airstrikes
Middle East.body: A report released Thursday examines the more than 500 Yemeni civilians its authors said were killed or wounded by US airstrikes in the Middle East nation during a recent 17-month period amid the open-ended so-called “War on Terror” that has left nearly one million people dead in around half a dozen nations over the past 25 years. The report – authored by the Yemen-based group Mwatana for Human Rights and published by the Costs of War Project at Brown University’s Watson Institute for International and Public Affairs – documents 46 US airstrikes that took place between December 2023 and May 2025 that caused at least 576 civilian casualties, including 213 deaths and 363 injuries. Americas.headline: Haitian bishop: ‘Enough is enough’ following Aug. 23 massacre
Americas.body: MIAMI | A shocking gang-related attack on a Haitian farming community drew a sharp reaction from a Haitian bishop currently living in South Florida following an act of mass murder and kidnapping. The Aug. 23 attack south of Haiti’s capital reportedly left as many as 47 people dead and some 50 more kidnapped, although the numbers, first reported by the United Nations, have not been fully verified. The attack began when armed members of the Viv Ansanm gang coalition descended on Kenscoff, setting homes ablaze, killing residents and abducting dozens, according to The Associated Press. Americas.headline: Colombia’s Earthquake History Teaches Property Buyers to Check the Building Code First
Americas.body: After the Earthquake: Investing in Colombia with Knowledge and Confidence Every time we feel an earthquake—even one that lasts only a few seconds—we are reminded of something we often take for granted: the safety of the place we call home. For anyone considering a real estate investment in Colombia, this concern is entirely understandable. Buying property is an important financial decision, but it also means choosing a place to live, build wealth or welcome other people. That is why investors should look beyond location, price and potential returns and also consider how and when the property was built. Colombia has developed its earthquake-resistant building regulations over several decades.

Africa.headline: DR Congo — Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 3,400 Deaths as Officials Claim Infection Peak
Africa.body: Government data from the Democratic Republic of the Congo indicates that the country's Ebola outbreak has grown to 7,200 confirmed cases and at least 3,475 deaths across seven provinces. More than 60 health zones are currently affected, with nearly 1,000 patients receiving treatment in isolation facilities. Official surveillance reports indicate that virus transmission peaked in mid-August as infection growth began to slow. However, public health experts emphasize that contact tracing remains at 88%, falling short of the threshold required to halt transmission, while response efforts remain constrained in eastern conflict-affected zones.

Africa.headline: Kenya — National Ebola High Alert Activated Amid Regional Outbreak
Africa.body: The Kenyan Ministry of Interior and National Administration has placed the country on high alert and activated the National Ebola Incident Management System as a precautionary measure against the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Officials confirmed that all suspected Ebola cases tested nationwide have returned negative results. Preparedness measures have been heightened across national and county levels, with four laboratories officially designated for diagnostic testing. The heightened surveillance measures coincide with ongoing efforts to contain local outbreaks of mpox, dengue, and measles.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Climate minister says repeated floods have displaced 40 million people in Pakistan
Asia-Pacific.body: - Musadik Malik says last five major floods killed around 7,000 people, injured or disabled 17,000 - PM orders disaster agencies to prepare for heavy rains, possible flooding during ongoing monsoon ISLAMABAD: Repeated floods have displaced around 40 million people in Pakistan, Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik said on Tuesday, describing how successive deluges were uprooting families from communities where they had lived for generations. Asia-Pacific.headline: UNICEF expands aid to millions of Afghan children after flash floods
Asia-Pacific.body: Flash floods affected more than 1,100 families across 14 provinces of Afghanistan in July, damaging or destroying over 1,100 homes, according to UNICEF’s latest humanitarian situation report covering July 1–31. UNICEF said 1,168 families were affected by the floods, while 1,164 homes were damaged or destroyed. In Parun, the capital of Nuristan province, 23 people were killed in flooding, while water services for around 1,000 families were disrupted. Despite the ongoing humanitarian challenges, UNICEF said it continued supporting essential health services across the country through 2,393 static health facilities and 16 mobile facilities. Asia-Pacific.body: Nepal Lost Its Power Plants To Floods: How India's 654 MW Lifeline Will Keep The Lights On The Indian Ministry of Power has approved the supply of power to Nepal from September 13 to December 31. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola epidemic expands as health agencies adapt tracking strategies
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: United Nations officials warned that the Ebola epidemic in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo remains massive and continues to grow in several areas, despite localized progress. According to UN and World Health Organization representatives, controlling the second most lethal Ebola outbreak on record will take months. To predict high-risk areas, health authorities are utilizing anonymized mobile phone data to monitor population movements, though telecom partnership constraints present challenges. Surveillance reporting indicates the outbreak has reached 7,200 confirmed cases and 3,475 deaths, with over 6,250 people affected since May.
